topic.title: Microcode Update (MCU)

body.p: IA-32 processors have the capability to correct specific errata through the loading of an Intel-supplied data block. This data block is referred to as a microcode update or system configuration data.

The Intel ® 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual describes the microcode update header, and the underlying mechanisms the BIOS or an OS CPU Driver needs to provide in order to utilize this feature during system initialization.

ul.li: Intel defines a processor, as the silicon and the accompanying microcode update.
Any processor that does not have a valid microcode update is considered by Intel to be operating out of spec and may not continue to boot.
It is BIOS's responsibility to ensure all logical processors (BSP and APs) in the system have the correct microcode update installed as soon as it wakes up.
A revision check before proceeding a microcode update load should always be in place for performance consideration.
Loading a debug microcode update requires the debug capability being enabled via a hardware mechanism (such as a jumper) or the IA32_DEBUG_INTERFACE MSR.
The microcode update size may various per processor SKU. BIOS is required to allocate adequate microcode update storage for each processor stepping as the system intent to support.
Extended Processor Signature verification is required.
